Actually class is package-private (no public) and methods are default (no public). JUnit 5 requires @Test on methods, but they can be package-private? I think JUnit 5 allows default visibility? I think it requires public? Actually JUnit 5 test classes and methods can be package-private, they just need to be annotated. However test runner found 0 tests. Possibly because the test class is not public and not annotated with @TestInstance? Wait JUnit 5 discovers test classes that are either public or package-private? I think it requires the class to be public. In JUnit 5, test classes can be package-private, but they must be annotated with @Test? The class itself doesn't need annotation. But maybe the test engine didn't pick up because the class is not public and not annotated with @Test? Actually JUnit Jupiter discovers test classes that are top-level classes that are either public or package-private? Quick recall: JUnit 5 requires test classes to be public? I think not, but maybe the test engine requires at least default constructor and not abstract. However the test runner says 0 tests found. Maybe because the @Test methods are not imported from JUnit Jupiter (org.junit.jupiter.api.Test) but from org.junit.Test (JUnit 4). Indeed the imports: import org.junit.Test; import org.junit.AfterClass; import org.junit.BeforeClass; import org.junit.Assert; Those are JUnit 4 annotations. But the test runner includes both JUnit Jupiter and Vintage, but the class uses JUnit 4 style. However the @BeforeClass and @AfterClass are commented out, but the @Test is JUnit4. JUnit Vintage should run them. But they are not static? In JUnit4, @BeforeClass and @AfterClass must be static, but they are static but commented out. The @Test methods are package-private (default) and not public. In JUnit4, test methods must be public. So they are not recognized. That's why 0 tests found.

Solution: make class public and methods public, and use JUnit5 annotations (org.junit.jupiter.api.Test) and proper imports. Also need to enable @BeforeAll and @AfterAll static methods and annotate them. Use JUnit5's @BeforeAll, @AfterAll.

Also need to adjust imports: remove JUnit4 imports, use JUnit5.

Also need to import Assertions from JUnit5 for assertTrue etc.

But they use Assert.assertEquals etc from JUnit4. Could keep using org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions static methods or keep JUnit4's Assert? JUnit5 can still use org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions, but JUnit4's Assert is also available. However test methods need to be public.

Simplify: change class to public, make methods public, import org.junit.jupiter.api.*; replace Assert with Assertions (or keep Assert). JUnit5's Assertions has assertEquals, assertTrue, fail.

Let's rewrite test class accordingly.

Also need to adjust usage of NaN class: org.ta4j.core.num.NaN is a subclass of Num. The test uses instanceof NaN; that's fine.

Potential other compile errors: NumericIndicator.of(indexIndicator()) expects Indicator<Num>. indexIndicator returns Indicator<Num>. Good.

Need to ensure NumericIndicator class exists in the library; we assume.

Make sure to import java.util.function.Function; not used now maybe.

Remove unused imports.
